text:
Response B has a factual error. It says the job "was stopped after 35 minutes", but the report says it was stopped at 9:35am. The first call came at 8:20am and the problem began earlier, so "35 minutes" is invented and understates how long the error ran. B also leaves out the leaked staff message and the news story, which a manager would probably want to know about. Otherwise B is tight, at about 105 words, within the limit.

Response A is accurate on every figure and date, and it includes the media angle and the comms guide fix. But it runs to roughly 175 words, well over the 120-word cap. It also pads with filler ("To give some background", "We would like to note", "Looking ahead", "Finally"), which adds nothing.

Accuracy comes first in the criteria. A has no factual errors, while B misstates the timing, and A keeps more of the points a manager needs. A's breach of the word limit is a real failing, but it does not outweigh B's inaccuracy under this ordering.

Verdict: A
